findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a concrete proving command to each of ACs 3, 4, 5, and 6 (e.g. `pytest … -k empty_path_does_not_abort`, an integration pytest invocation with an event-set length assertion for AC4, `pytest … -k full_success_golden`, and a `grep`-based doc content check for AC6).
evidence: AC3: 'A path whose blame legitimately yields zero lines does not abort the derivation. Tier: unit.' — no pytest invocation.
AC4: 'No caused_by link event is written in that case. Tier: integration on the close path asserting the event set.' — no pytest or integration command.
AC5: 'With all paths succeeding, the derived culprit is unchanged from today — the negative control. Tier: unit golden comparison.' — no pytest invocation.

AC6: 'The guidance doc exists, states the measured numbers, names the accepted git blame degradation, and is linked from the docs index. Tier: doc-existence + content check.' — no grep/ls/doc-lint command.
ACs 1 and 2 both supply a `pytest … -k <name> -v` command; the absence of equivalent commands for ACs 3–6 is a structural inconsistency, not an inference gap.
findings.finding: ACs 3, 4, 5, and 6 each state a tier and an outcome but supply no concrete proving command, leaving an executor without a deterministic way to confirm those four criteria are met.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC3 (zero-line negative control), AC4 (no caused_by link event written), AC5 (golden comparison), AC6 (doc-existence + content check)
scenarios: An executor writing AC3's test has no canonical filter pattern to target, so CI cannot pin the criterion to a specific test name.
AC4 is the only integration-level criterion (exercises the live close path); without a command an auditor cannot confirm the event set is asserted rather than merely described.
AC5's golden-comparison test has no named filter, so a reviewer cannot confirm the regression guard actually runs.
AC6 has no shell check (e.g. grep for the measured numbers in the doc file), so doc-existence and content can be declared done without machine-verifiable evidence.
findings.suggested_fix:
AC3: `pytest tests/unit/metrics/test_blame.py -k empty_path_does_not_abort -v`
AC4: `pytest tests/integration/metrics/test_blame_close.py -k no_caused_by_on_partial_failure -v` (assert `caused_by` absent from returned event set)
AC5: `pytest tests/unit/metrics/test_blame.py -k full_success_golden -v`
AC6: `grep -E '68\.7 MiB|14\.3 s|1\.04 GiB|59 s|blob:none|tree:0' docs/<filename>.md && grep -r '<filename>' docs/index.md`

AC6 says 'linked from the docs index' without naming which file is the docs index (e.g. `docs/index.md`, `docs/README.md`, or a mkdocs nav).
findings.finding: The doc AC does not specify the filename or sub-path within `docs/` for the new guidance page, nor does it name the docs-index file — an executor must guess both, risking placing the document in the wrong location or linking to the wrong index.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC6 (doc-existence + content check); Files section (`docs/` guidance page)

Two executors working from the plan independently pick different filenames, making the doc-existence grep command in a child ticket invalid.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Files section: `docs/clone-guide.md` (new file); update AC6 to read '…linked from `docs/index.md`'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace AC5's 'golden comparison / unchanged from today' with a behaviorally specified unit test: given a concrete fixture (explicit fake blame output per path, known commit SHAs), assert `derive_caused_by` returns the specific expected SHA — not 'same as before'.
evidence: 'unchanged from today' — output is snapshotted against the current implementation's result, not against an independently specified expected value
'golden comparison' — explicit snapshot/serialization language
If derive_caused_by has any latent bug on the happy path, this test codifies it as correct behavior
findings.finding: AC5 specifies a 'golden comparison' (snapshot of current output) to verify the happy path is unchanged, which is the change-detector anti-pattern — it locks in whatever `derive_caused_by` currently produces rather than asserting a behaviorally specified expected value from concrete inputs.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC5: 'the derived culprit is unchanged from today — the negative control. Tier: unit golden comparison.'
scenarios: A latent happy-path bug in the existing derive_caused_by logic gets locked in by the snapshot, making it invisible to future fixes
The snapshot is authored by running the current (possibly wrong) code, creating a tautological oracle
findings.suggested_fix: Define a small self-contained fixture in the test file: e.g., two paths each blaming commits A and B (A majority), assert derive_caused_by returns A. This is independently verifiable and does not snapshot live code output.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC (and implementation note) requiring that when `derive_caused_by` suppresses a result due to per-path blame failure, a structured log warning (or metric increment) is emitted so operators can observe the degradation.
evidence: AC #4 only asserts the event set does not contain a caused_by link; no AC or plan prose specifies that a warning/error is logged or a metric is incremented when derivation is suppressed
'derive_caused_by returns None when _blame_file_commits returns None for any path' — silent return with no observability hook
'Partial failure is not [benign]' — the plan acknowledges the risk but specifies no operator-visible signal for when it occurs
ABSENCE: no mention of logging, metrics, alerting, or tracing in any plan section
findings.finding: When `derive_caused_by` aborts due to a per-path `_blame_file_commits` returning `None`, no log entry, metric, or trace is specified — operators have no visibility into silent blame-failure degradation in production.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC #4 ('No caused_by link event is written in that case') and 'The code fix' section
scenarios: A production blobless clone silently suppresses `caused_by` derivations for weeks; no alert fires; data quality degrades invisibly
A partly-warm object store causes intermittent partial failures; without a log line the on-call engineer cannot distinguish 'no culprit found' from 'blame faulted'
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Acceptance Criteria: '- [ ] When `derive_caused_by` returns `None` due to a `_blame_file_commits` failure, a `logger.warning("blame partial failure: %s", path)` (or equivalent metric) is emitted. Tier: unit, assert log record present.' In `blame.py`, before returning `None`, call `logger.warning("git blame failed for path %s; aborting caused_by derivation", path)`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Audit ALL callers of `_blame_file_commits` (not just `derive_caused_by`), document each one's handling of the new `None` return, and add an explicit rollback/back-out step (e.g., 'revert commit X' or an expand-contract sequence) in case the changed semantics cause an undetected breakage in production.
evidence: Plan states: '_blame_file_commits returns None on git failure and [] on a successful-but-empty result' — this is a return-type contract change
Plan names only one consumer path: `derive_caused_by` via `blame.py:94` and `transition_close.py:514`
No rollback path, feature flag, or expand-contract sequence is specified for the return-type change
Rubric: 'The remedy for a destructive/breaking change is an explicit ROLLBACK / back-out plan or expand-contract sequencing — checking only that breakage is acknowledged is insufficient'
findings.finding: The plan changes `_blame_file_commits`'s return contract from `list` (always) to `Optional[list]` — a breaking interface change — but does not enumerate all callers beyond `derive_caused_by`, nor provide an explicit rollback or back-out plan if the changed semantics break an unconsidered call site (e.g., a caller that does `for x in _blame_file_commits(...)` would raise `TypeError` on `None` rather than behaving as before).
findings.location: ## The code fix — 'This ticket must therefore FIRST change `_blame_file_commits`…'
scenarios: An unaudited second caller of `_blame_file_commits` iterates the result directly; after the change it receives `None` and raises `TypeError` at runtime
A rollback is needed but the team has no documented procedure, so a wrong `caused_by` write continues until manually corrected
findings.suggested_fix: Add a section 'Rollback plan: revert commits A–B (return-type change + derive_caused_by guard) atomically; no data migration needed as no schema changes are made.' Also add a grep/search step in the PR checklist: `grep -rn '_blame_file_commits' src/` to confirm no other callers exist before merging.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Explicitly confirm (in the plan or via an AC) that `transition_close.py:514` already handles a `None` return from `derive_caused_by` without crashing — e.g., by citing the existing None-guard inherited from the total-failure path — so the caller's safety is specified, not merely implied by the integration AC outcome.
evidence: Plan states: 'derive_caused_by loops per path and tallies across all of them... can elect a culprit that would not have won over the full set. That writes a wrong caused_by link'
Plan states AC4: 'No caused_by link event is written in that case. Tier: integration on the close path asserting the event set'
Plan names the caller explicitly: 'transition_close.py:514' but does not describe what that caller does with a None return from derive_caused_by
Plan notes 'Total failure is benign (blame.py:37 returns None)' but does not explicitly extend this to derive_caused_by returning None into transition_close.py
E3(d) requires: 'where the plan changes existing behavior, it acknowledges callers that depend on the old behavior'
findings.finding: The plan changes `derive_caused_by`'s return-value contract (from a potentially-wrong culprit to `None` on partial blame failure) but does not explicitly confirm that `transition_close.py:514` — the named caller — handles a `None` return without crashing or producing a silent no-op that differs from the old wrong-answer behavior. AC4 asserts the outcome ('no caused_by link event is written') without stating the mechanism by which `transition_close.py` achieves it.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — AC4 / 'The code fix' section referencing transition_close.py:514
scenarios: If transition_close.py:514 does not guard against None from derive_caused_by (e.g., attempts to use the result unconditionally), the new behavior causes a runtime crash rather than a silent no-op — observable as an unhandled exception on every bug-close event that hits a partial blame failure.
If transition_close.py:514 silently swallows None but the integration test is written incorrectly (testing the wrong event type), the wrong-answer bug could persist undetected despite AC4 passing.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence under 'The code fix': 'transition_close.py:514 already guards against None from derive_caused_by (the same guard that handles the total-failure path at blame.py:37), so no change is needed there; AC4's integration test confirms the guard fires correctly.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `scripts/backfill_caused_by.py` to the Files section and confirm (or explicitly note) that its existing `if culprit_id is None: continue` guard already handles the new abort-on-partial-failure behavior correctly.
evidence: scripts/backfill_caused_by.py:28: `from rebar.metrics.blame import derive_caused_by`
scripts/backfill_caused_by.py:43: `culprit_id = derive_caused_by(bug_id, repo_root, tracker_dir)`
The plan's Files section lists only `src/rebar/metrics/blame.py`, `docs/` guidance page, and tests — `scripts/backfill_caused_by.py` is absent.
The plan body discusses only `transition_close.py:514` as the call-site consumer; `backfill_caused_by.py` is never mentioned.
findings.finding: `scripts/backfill_caused_by.py` is an unenumerated consumer of `derive_caused_by` (outside `src/rebar/metrics/`) that the plan does not list in its Files section or acknowledge anywhere.
scenarios: A reviewer verifying the plan's edit set will miss that `backfill_caused_by.py` exercises `derive_caused_by` in a loop over all closed bugs — the behavioral change (aborting on partial failure) affects this script's output too, even though `None`-handling is already correct.
If any future AC or integration test targets 'all consumers of derive_caused_by behave correctly after the change', the backfill script will be missed.
findings.suggested_fix: Append `scripts/backfill_caused_by.py` to the Files list and add a note in the plan body: 'The backfill script already handles `None` at line 44 (`if culprit_id is None: continue`), so no code change is required there, but the behavioral change means previously-emitted wrong culprit links will not be retroactively corrected by a re-run — operators should be aware.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a one-sentence positive rationale in the 'code fix' section explaining why sentinel `None` (rather than, e.g., a raised exception) was chosen for `_blame_file_commits` — e.g., that it preserves the module's best-effort, never-raise contract and keeps the only call site a simple `if result is None: return None` check.
evidence: The plan states WHAT to do ('change `_blame_file_commits` to return `None` on git failure and `[]` on a successful-but-empty result') but not WHY this interface shape was preferred.

No positive rationale section exists; the closest text ('Treating a legitimately empty file as a failure would suppress correct derivations') justifies the two-value distinction in general but not the specific sentinel-None mechanism over alternatives.
G6 rubric: 'The plan states a POSITIVE rationale for the chosen approach (its absence is a finding)'.
findings.finding: The plan specifies the sentinel-`None` approach for `_blame_file_commits` but provides no positive rationale for why this design was chosen over structurally different alternatives (e.g., raising a domain exception from `_blame_file_commits` and catching it in `derive_caused_by`, or wrapping the git call in a result-type). Without a stated rationale, a future reviewer cannot confirm the design decision was deliberate or evaluate whether it remains appropriate if the function gains additional call sites.
findings.location: Plan section: 'The code fix' / `_blame_file_commits` change description
scenarios: An implementer encountering an existing codebase convention of raising exceptions for git failures could reasonably choose a different approach without the plan's guidance.
If `_blame_file_commits` later gains a second call site, the caller must know to check for `None` — a rationale note would signal this contract is intentional.
findings.suggested_fix: Append to the 'The code fix' section: 'Sentinel `None` is chosen over raising an exception because it preserves the module-wide best-effort contract (callers never need try/except around blame helpers) and keeps the change self-contained within the one call site in `derive_caused_by`.'

findings.finding: The plan cites `transition_close.py:513` as the location where `derive_caused_by` is called, but reading the file shows line 513 is a blank line; the actual call `culprit = blame.derive_caused_by(...)` is at line 514. This is an off-by-one in a cited line number that is directly verifiable.
findings.location: Plan section 'The code fix (why it belongs with the doc)': '… <- transition_close.py:513'
findings.suggested_fix: Change `transition_close.py:513` → `transition_close.py:514` in the 'The code fix' section.

findings.finding: _blame_file_commits currently returns [] for BOTH a git failure (line 71: `if out is None: return []`) AND a legitimate empty file (no lines parsed from successful git output). The plan's fix — 'abort on any per-path blame failure' — cannot be implemented correctly without first changing _blame_file_commits's return contract to return None on failure vs. [] on success-with-no-lines. Without that prerequisite change, an implementer treating [] as failure would incorrectly abort on empty files; treating [] as success leaves the bug unfixed. The plan specifies only the derive_caused_by behavior and does not mention this required change to the helper's signature.
findings.location: Code fix section / src/rebar/metrics/blame.py:67-71 (_blame_file_commits) and derive_caused_by loop at :109
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Files/code-fix section: '_blame_file_commits signature changes to `-> list[str] | None`; it returns `None` when `_git` returns `None` (any git/OS failure) and `[]` when git succeeds but the file has no lines. `derive_caused_by` checks `if _blame_file_commits(...) is None: return None`.' The AC unit-test injecting a per-path failure should inject a None return from _blame_file_commits (not []) to keep the empty-file case as a separate passing scenario.

findings.finding: `_blame_file_commits` currently returns `[]` for BOTH a git failure and a genuinely empty file — there is no failure sentinel distinguishable from success. The plan's AC1 fix ('return None when _blame_file_commits fails for any path') cannot be implemented inside `derive_caused_by` alone without first changing `_blame_file_commits` to return `None` on failure vs `[]` on success. The plan's Files list only names `blame.py`, which is correct, but the internal signature change to `_blame_file_commits` is not called out anywhere.
findings.location: `src/rebar/metrics/blame.py:67-79` (`_blame_file_commits`) + AC line 1 ('derive_caused_by returns None when _blame_file_commits fails for any path')
findings.suggested_fix: In the code-fix section, add: '`_blame_file_commits` will be changed to return `list[str] | None` — `None` on any git error, `[]` only for a genuinely empty blame output — so `derive_caused_by` can reliably detect per-path failure and return `None` early.'
